Delicious and interesting restaurant
Nov 2018 • Solo
I was staying not far from this restaurant and wanted to check in out. The menu is large and I wanted to try more dishes than I could possibly eat. There are pictures of the dishes on the menu. The staff spoke limited English and I saw no other foreigners when I was there. 
I had fried abalone mushrooms with tofu and veggies, a large avocado salad with mango and a delicious rice soup with tofu skins. I also tried the banana blossom rolls. I've become very fond of banana blossoms. Really great! I could not eat it all and the price is very, very reasonable. 
As I finished eating, a Vietnamese monk stopped to say hello to me and asked how I liked it. Turns out that he lives in Colorado. We discussed Buddhist practice and vegetarian food. Interesting and engaging for me.

Nice food
Nov 2018 • Friends
This is the 2nd time I came to this restaurant. The food is nice, tasty and well presented.
The sauce is so light and doesn’t have the strong smell of the fermented tofu sauce but you can still taste it and cannot faulted.
The only thing that why I cannot give a 5 stars is the lack of air conditioning in Saigon. For local people is ok but for tourist it is like have lunch/dinner in a sauna. Ok I may exaggerate a bit but the heat is unpleasant to fully enjoy the food.

But if you don’t mind the heat, this is a restaurant you should not miss.

Do not eat here. Better vegan/veggie restaurants all around town
May 2017 • Couples
I just ate here for lunch because I saw this restaurant while driving by. It looked so beautiful on the outside. I went in to order food and no one was really friendly or attentive. The inside of the restaurant felt quite old and nasty (especially compared to the new signs on the outside). We ordered two fried rice dishes with okra. It was unbelievable what they charged and gave for the dishes. One rice was literally steamed rice with the thinnest slice of Tofu and a shredded fake meat with tiny slices of onions. Three of the thinnest slices of tomato and cucumber. I believe the rice dish was about 60,000 VND... unbelievable. It didn't taste that great either. I've lived in HCM for more than two years and this was one of the most disappointing vegetarian/vegan restaurant experiences I've had.

Vajra restaurant is literally within walking distance of this restaurant(near Ba Thang Hai) and one million times better all around. I would have normally eaten there, but I wanted to try something new and it was a big fail today.

Save yourself and don't even bother eating here...
